description: Held-out U.S. history sentence-to-evidence alignment benchmark. Each case pairs a manuscript sentence with a candidate source chunk and labels whether the chunk lexically supports the sentence. Used to calibrate the lexical-overlap threshold consumed by validate_sentence_evidence_alignment().

cases.sentence: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
cases.source_chunk: Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776, in Philadelphia.
cases.review_notes: Source restates the claim with explicit date and location.

cases.sentence: The American Civil War ended in 1865.
cases.source_chunk: Hostilities of the American Civil War concluded in 1865 when Confederate forces surrendered at Appomattox.
cases.review_notes: Same named conflict, same end year, supporting causal detail.

cases.sentence: Apollo 11 landed astronauts on the Moon in 1969.
cases.source_chunk: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 successfully placed two astronauts on the lunar surface.
cases.review_notes: Lunar surface paraphrases Moon; year and mission identifier match.

cases.sentence: The Bill of Rights was ratified in 1791.
cases.source_chunk: The first ten amendments, known as the Bill of Rights, were ratified by the states in 1791.
cases.review_notes: Identical ratification year for the same instrument.

cases.sentence: The Marshall Plan provided economic aid to Europe.
cases.source_chunk: Marshall Plan disbursed economic assistance to European nations recovering from the war.
cases.review_notes: Aid vs. assistance is a synonym swap; topic and recipients align.

cases.sentence: Franklin Roosevelt launched the New Deal in 1933.
cases.source_chunk: Beginning in 1933, President Roosevelt rolled out a sweeping set of New Deal programs aimed at recovery.
cases.review_notes: Different verb (launched vs. rolled out) but same principal, year, and policy name.

cases.sentence: The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776.
cases.source_chunk: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March in 44 BC by a group of Roman senators.
cases.review_notes: Completely different topic and era — should not align.

cases.sentence: The Nineteenth Amendment granted women the right to vote.
cases.source_chunk: The Apollo program required massive funding from the federal government during the 1960s.
cases.review_notes: Source is about space funding, not suffrage.

cases.sentence: The Vietnam War lasted nearly two decades.
cases.source_chunk: The Korean War concluded with an armistice in 1953 after three years of fighting.
cases.review_notes: Both are Cold War conflicts but the source describes a different war.

cases.sentence: The Treaty of Versailles formally ended World War I.
cases.source_chunk: The Treaty of Paris in 1783 ended the American Revolutionary War with British recognition of independence.
cases.review_notes: Shared 'treaty' and 'war' tokens make this a lexical-overlap trap; verifier must rely on entity-specific cues.

cases.sentence: The U.S. Constitution was ratified in 1788.
cases.source_chunk: The U.S. Constitution was drafted at the Philadelphia Convention in 1787 before going to the states for ratification.
cases.review_notes: Same document but the chunk reports drafting, not ratification, and a different year.

cases.sentence: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States.
cases.source_chunk: The Hoover Dam was completed during the Great Depression in 1936 along the Colorado River.
cases.review_notes: No shared named entities; topic mismatch.
